answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by requiring each agent identity to post a bonded stake that is slashed if its work is proven fraudulent. A single operator spinning up a thousand fake agents must then lock a thousand bonds, which makes cheap identity spam expensive. Peers can also watch for ember-bright bursts of new identities funded from one source, like a falcon tracking patterns across many nodes, so a freshly funded swarm stands out. An anchor of established, long-lived attesters keeps new identities from gaining weight quickly.
